summary: Describes an inter-domain VPLS solution that provides provider edge node redundancy across domains, avoiding service interruption when a single domain has no redundancy.

eli5.summary: If a bridge between two cities fails, there should be a spare. This gives both sides a backup route.

questions: what is a vpls redundancy group
how does iccp help vpls failover
subtitle: How two VPLS networks can back each other up with redundant edge routers using existing ICCP and pseudowire tools.

tldr.problem: In many inter-domain VPLS deployments, pseudowire connectivity gives no Provider Edge (PE) redundancy, or gives it in only one domain, so one failure can interrupt service.
tldr.mechanism: Redundant PEs in each domain form a redundancy group, coordinate over ICCP, and negotiate which pseudowire is active using the PW Preferential Forwarding Status Bit. No new messages or protocol options are added.
tldr.outcome: PE node and link redundancy in both domains, with faster failover than relying on BGP convergence. It only works if both operators provision it consistently.

today: RFC 7309 is a Proposed Standard published in July 2014. It is not marked as obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: Why Inter-domain VPLS Needs Redundancy
sections.content:
Inter-AS Virtual Private LAN Service (VPLS) is widely deployed, and the border routers and links between domains carry many services, so PE node and link redundancy matter for service level agreements. The RFC builds on RFC 4762 VPLS, where a domain means an autonomous system or another administrative domain.

Existing options have drawbacks. Inter-AS option A (RFC 4364) with MC-LAG and ICCP needs Ethernet links of the same speed, which rules out cases such as packet over SONET/SDH. MP-BGP (RFC 6074, options B or C) depends on BGP control-plane convergence, which may be too slow for tight SLAs, and is not always deployed for VPLS.

The RFC also argues for better multicast behavior than option B when label switched multicast is not used (RFC 7117): each PE replicates only to local PEs and the ASBR, and the remote ASBR replicates onward, spreading the load.
sections.eli5: The older ways of adding a spare needed matching roads, or were slow to notice a problem. This way works over different kinds of links and reacts faster.

sections.title: The Building Blocks and Use Cases
sections.content:
The solution reuses existing pieces: the Inter-Chassis Communication Protocol (ICCP, RFC 7275) to coordinate the two redundant edge nodes, and the PW Preferential Forwarding Status Bit (RFC 6870) to negotiate pseudowire status. The RFC states that no protocol message formats change and no new options are introduced; it describes how to reuse these blocks and the implementation behavior required.

Two PE nodes in each domain form a redundancy group (RG). The PEs may be ASBRs or ordinary VPLS PEs. Two use cases are described: two inter-domain pseudowires (one active, one standby), and four pseudowires connecting every PE in one RG to every PE in the other.

Both pseudowire redundancy modes from RFC 6718 apply. Independent mode is preferred by operators because it keeps the control planes of the two domains separate; master/slave mode adds enhanced capabilities.
sections.eli5: Each town has two gatekeepers who talk to each other all day. The towns reuse rules they already have for deciding who is on duty.

sections.title: Switchover Conditions
sections.content:
The RFC adds three ICCP switchover conditions to the PW redundancy procedure of RFC 7275. In each, the PE that takes over is the one with the highest priority after the failing PE.

  • Inter-domain PW failure: when the active PE advertises that all its inter-domain PWs are DOWN or STANDBY, the next PE SHOULD advertise active for all its inter-domain PWs.
  • PE node isolation: a PE that loses all PWs to its local domain SHOULD advertise standby on all its inter-domain PWs, which triggers the remote PE to switch over.
  • PE node failure: if a PE detects that the active PE in its RG has gone down, and it has redundant PWs for the affected services, it SHOULD advertise active.

For the four-PW scenario, both ICCP peers in an RG must support the same redundancy mode, which can be ensured by manual configuration.
sections.eli5: If the gatekeeper on duty falls ill, loses the road, or cannot be reached, the next gatekeeper in line steps up and tells everyone.

sections.title: Two-PW and Four-PW Redundancy
sections.content:
Two PWs: ICCP runs on the edge nodes in both domains, using independent mode only and 1:1 protection (1 standby, 1 active). The operators must agree on matching high or low PW priority at the two endpoints; in the RFC's example, PE3 and PE5 must both have higher or both lower priority than PE4 and PE6, otherwise both PWs end up standby.

Four PWs, 1:1: independent mode only, with no priority coordination between operators. A PE that sees one PW DOWN sets the other to STANDBY if available and syncs this to its ICCP peer.

Four PWs, 3:1 (3 standby, 1 active): implementations MUST support option A and MAY support option B. In option A, ICCP runs in both domains in independent mode with the Request Switchover bit. On failure the PE switches to another local standby PW and sets 'request switchover' on it. If both ends request at once, the PE with the higher IP address ignores the request and the lower one clears its bit and sets 'Preferential Forwarding'. In option B, ICCP runs in only one domain, master/slave mode is used, and operators must agree which domain is master.
sections.eli5: With two roads, the towns must agree beforehand which is the main one. With four roads, the gatekeepers can sort it out themselves, and if both ask at once, the one with the higher street number waits.

sections.title: Management Considerations
sections.content: Consistent provisioning is required. Both domains must use the same use case (two PWs or four PWs), and all modes and options within it must be provisioned identically within each RG and between the RGs. For the two-PW case, the operators must also negotiate matching high or low PW priority at the two PW endpoints. If provisioning is inconsistent, the mechanism may not work properly.
sections.eli5: Both towns must follow the same plan. If one thinks there are two roads and the other thinks four, things go wrong.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The security properties of RFC 7275 for the ICCP control plane, and of RFC 4762 and RFC 6870 for the PW control plane, apply. ICCP runs between two PEs or ASBRs, which should be connected only by a well-managed network whose service levels and availability are highly monitored; the operator should ensure this.

Flapping of inter-domain or intra-domain PW state could create security threats or be exploited for denial of service, for example by a malicious peer's implementation causing excessive ICCP exchanges. Implementations SHOULD provide control-plane policing to mitigate such attacks.
sections.eli5: If someone keeps flipping the gatekeepers' signals on and off, everyone gets busy and overwhelmed, so the gatekeepers should be able to ignore too many signals.

items.title: Two PWs
items.text: Independent mode only, 1:1 protection; operators agree PW priorities.

items.title: Four PWs, 1:1
items.text: Independent mode only; no priority coordination between operators.

items.title: Four PWs, 3:1 option A
items.text: Independent mode with the request switchover bit; MUST be supported.

items.title: Four PWs, 3:1 option B
items.text: Master/slave mode, ICCP in one domain only; MAY be supported.
